tagline.text: A 3 km shoreline of smooth stones, 30 minutes from Surigao City

location.label: Location
location.text: Coast of Barangays Mabua, Ipil and Looc, Surigao City, Surigao del Norte

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱300–1,200 (half day from the city, covering transport, entrance, cottage and snacks)

children.text: This is a pebble beach about 3 km long that runs along the barangays of Mabua, Ipil and Looc on the east side of Surigao City. Smooth stones replace the sand, making it a pleasant place to walk, as if on a foot massage, beside clear water and a good sunset, and it takes about 30 minutes from the city by tricycle.

Many people pass through Surigao City only on the way to Siargao or the Dinagat Islands, but there is also a beach close to the city. It is a pebble beach about 3 km long that stretches across the three barangays of Mabua, Ipil and Looc on the city's east coast, and it is commonly called Mabua Pebble Beach. Local media explain that the shore is strictly speaking made of stones rather than pebbles, but among travelers the name Pebble Beach has stuck.

The charm of this beach is its unusual scenery, where round, smooth stones shaped by the waves take the place of a sandy shore. The water is clear and cool, good for a dip and for wading in the shallows, and many reviews describe walking barefoot on the stones as a natural foot massage. On the other hand, it is not a soft sand beach, and some say it is uncomfortable to lie on for long, so bringing a folding mat or beach sandals helps. The stones get very hot at midday, so the afternoon is better.

Resorts, cottages and small stores are scattered along the beach, and places with their own entrances charge different fees. Some guides say this public beach has no entrance or parking fee while others report up to about ₱100 at resort entrances, so expect free to about ₱100 depending on where you enter. Blogs from 2018–2023 put cottages at about ₱300–500 and up, and there is no official price list. The city prohibits taking stones, so please do not pocket one or two as souvenirs.

For planning, it works best to use Surigao City as your base and spend only half a day here. Arriving in the afternoon, swimming and staying for the sunset makes good use of your time, and if you have more days you can add nearby Basul Island, the Day-asan floating village or Siargao. Prices and operating details depend on when each review was written, so check current information locally. Surigao City is rainy, so a shower can come during the day; bring an umbrella or a light rain jacket. Even on cloudy days the pebble beach has atmosphere and photographs well, but sunset on a clear day is the most impressive.
A shoreline of round stones runs across the three barangays of Mabua, Ipil and Looc. The mood differs from stretch to stretch, so walk and choose the spot you like.
The water is clear and cool, good for swimming or dipping your feet in the shallows. Waves and currents vary with the weather, so check local conditions.
Reviews say that walking barefoot on the smooth stones feels like a foot massage. The stones get hot at midday and can burn your feet, so walk in the afternoon.
The sunset, as the sky shifts from blue to red and orange, is considered the biggest sight. Some accounts say the view from the rocks at the north end of the beach is best.
You can enjoy light activities such as volleyball, Frisbee and kayaking on the beach. Ask the resort about equipment.

Renting a nipa hut beside the water to eat lunch and snacks is the usual way to enjoy the beach. Blogs from 2018–2023 put cottages at about ₱300–500 and up. It tends to be quiet on weekdays and crowded with local families on weekends. Bring food or buy simple things at the store.

It is about 30 minutes from town by tricycle, so it is a good trip when you have time between connections. The airport is reported to be about 10 minutes from the city. Even a layover of only three or four hours is enough to walk the beach, see the sunset and return.

Return transport can be scarce, so agree on a waiting time with your driver in advance. On weekends and holidays, when the beach is crowded, arriving in the early afternoon makes it easier to get a good cottage. To photograph the sunset, take a spot on the rocks at the north end of the beach 30 minutes before the sun goes down.

Counting the connection from Manila, the trip can take almost a day, so allow plenty of time.

If you have a vehicle, enter Mabua Pebble Beach in your map app. One review says to get off at Mt. Bagarabon resort and walk to the beach.
Reviews also mention renting a small fishing boat (banca) to approach the beach from the sea.

Taxis and shared vans are not common, so agree on a round-trip fare with a tricycle driver at your lodging or the terminal. Some drivers quote a fare that includes waiting time. The beach has several entrances, so deciding in advance which resort to get off at will keep you from wandering.

In Surigao, December to February is described as relatively cool and November to April as the dry season, but there are also records of frequent rain around December. April is known as the month with the least rainfall, so check the forecast before you leave.
The afternoon is the best time of day. The stones are very hot at midday, and if you stay late until sunset, both the scenery and the temperature are comfortable.

On weekends and holidays, more local families visit and cottages fill first. Weekday afternoons are quieter, and during peak times such as Holy Week and the May school break, lodging in the city also fills up early, so book ahead.

There are resorts and cottages near the beach, and reviews mention a mountain resort and hotel at Mt. Bagarabon. Names and rates change, so check recent reviews on a map app. Most visitors stay in Surigao City and come for half a day at a time.

Reviews mention Surigao City hotels such as Parkway Hotel, Hotel Tavern Surigao, Philippine Gateway Hotel and Ey Miner Suites. Near the beach you can get snacks and drinks from stores, but the menu is limited, so eat lunch in the city or pack a meal.

You can easily find grilled seafood, coconut dishes and simple Filipino home cooking. Buying fresh fruit and snacks at the city market is also a good idea. Take your food and trash back with you, and do not harm the environment.

There are other places to see around Surigao City besides the beach. Basul Island, about 15 minutes by boat from Punta Bilang-bilang, is reported to charge about ₱50 entrance, about ₱100 docking and about ₱500 for a cottage, and the Day-asan floating village, about 7 km from the city, is a village of stilt houses built among mangroves. Laswitan Lagoon is reported to charge about ₱30 and be open from 7 AM to 5 PM. These prices come from 2022 reviews, so confirm current rates locally. Combining one or two of these with Mabua beach in a day makes a full Surigao itinerary.
A folding mat and a cushion make it more comfortable to sit on the stones.
Beach sandals or aqua shoes are safer. Avoid going barefoot when the stones are hot.
The sunset begins around 5:30 PM, so arrange your ride back in advance.
Do not take stones. The city tourism office prohibits removing them.
Bring plenty of food, drinks and water, and take your trash back with you.
Bring cash. Cards are hard to use at the beach stores and cottages.
Bring a power bank. Photos and maps use a lot of battery.
Ask the resort first about using equipment such as kayaks or volleyballs.
It is not confirmed whether lifeguards are present, and waves and currents change with the weather. Swim only in shallow water, and do not enter the sea when a typhoon is approaching.
The stones at midday are very hot and can burn your feet, so go in the afternoon or wear sandals.
Wet stones are slippery and may have sharp edges, so take care when moving about.
Transport is scarce, and not finding a ride back would be a real problem. Arrange a round trip before you come.
Entrance and cottage rates differ from place to place, so confirm them before you arrive.
The roads get dark after sunset, so return to the city soon after the sun goes down.
The Surigao coast is an earthquake-prone area near the Philippine Trench. If you feel strong shaking, move to higher ground and follow local instructions.
The surfing island reached by boat from Surigao. Confirm ports and boat schedules locally, and allow plenty of time.
Islands off Surigao that are good for island tours and beach relaxation. Confirm boat schedules locally.
A multi-tiered waterfall in Surigao del Sur that can be linked with the beach on a longer trip. The travel time is long, so plan a full day.
A river famous for its emerald-colored swimming spot. It is more than half a day's trip from Surigao City.
